theme: Core Data under the hood: the store, faults and migration

terms.definition: The file on disk where the framework keeps all of the saved objects.
terms.example: The persistent store is a single SQLite file.
terms.code:
import CoreData
let d = NSPersistentStoreDescription()
d.type = NSSQLiteStoreType
print(d.type)

terms.definition: A lazy loading trick that keeps a light placeholder until you actually read the object's data.
terms.example: Faulting keeps memory low because data loads only when needed.

terms.definition: An automatic update of the saved data to a new model, when the changes are simple, such as adding a field.
terms.example: Turn on lightweight migration for the new field.
terms.code:
import CoreData
let d = NSPersistentStoreDescription()
d.shouldMigrateStoreAutomatically = true
d.shouldInferMappingModelAutomatically = true
print(d.shouldInferMappingModelAutomatically)

video.title: Persistent Store, Faulting & Lightweight Migration | Day 215
video.description:
Learn to explain where Core Data keeps data, how it loads it lazily and how it updates old data: Persistent Store, Faulting & Lightweight Migration, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Persistent Store - The file on disk where the framework keeps all of the saved objects.
Faulting - A lazy loading trick that keeps a light placeholder until you actually read the object's data.
Lightweight Migration - An automatic update of the saved data to a new model, when the changes are simple, such as adding a field.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: iOS Persistent Store, Faulting & Lightweight Migration | Day 215
landscape.description:
Explain Persistent Store, Faulting & Lightweight Migration in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Persistent Store, Faulting, Lightweight Migration 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Persistent Store - The file on disk where the framework keeps all of the saved objects.
한국어: Persistent Store: 저장된 객체를 모두 보관하는 디스크 위의 파일

Faulting - A lazy loading trick that keeps a light placeholder until you actually read the object's data.
한국어: Faulting: 객체의 데이터를 실제로 읽기 전까지 가벼운 자리 표시자만 두는 지연 로딩 기법

Lightweight Migration - An automatic update of the saved data to a new model, when the changes are simple, such as adding a field.
한국어: Lightweight Migration: 필드 추가처럼 변경이 단순할 때 저장된 데이터를 새 모델로 자동 변환하는 방식

landscape.hook: Can you explain Persistent Store, Faulting and Lightweight Migration in English?

dialogue.title: The update that broke the store

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, users who update the app get a crash on launch.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did you change the model? Old data sits in the persistent store, in the old shape.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Where is the persistent store, exactly?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It is a file on disk. Core Data reads the saved objects from it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And the new field does not match that file.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. You need lightweight migration. It updates the old data to the new model.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Lightweight migration works for simple changes, like a new field.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Also, why does `isFault` return true for some objects?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is faulting. Core Data keeps a light placeholder and loads the data later.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Faulting is normal, so do not worry about it.
The persistent store is one file on disk.
